skills.import.emptyDir: Folder name {dir} is empty once lowercased and stripped of spaces: import it with a new name (rename)
skills.import.renamed: Imported under a new name: originally {original}
skills.import.reservedCollection: A collection can't be called {reserved} (/skill:folder is how you invoke a skill, so it would be ambiguous): pick another name
skills.import.collectionNameTaken: Collection name {name} clashes with {owner}: pick another name
skills.import.collectionDirTaken: The skills area already has a folder called {name}: pick another collection name, or move that folder away first
skills.import.noMembers: No folders with a SKILL.md under {root} (if the members aren't directly under the root, give the subfolder they're in)
skills.import.notValid: Not a valid skill, not imported: {problem}
skills.import.emptyMemberDir: Folder name {dir} is empty once lowercased and stripped of spaces, not imported (you can import it with a new name: collection.rename)
skills.conflict.sameDir: {name} in this collection (folder {dir}): both folder names become {finalDir}
skills.conflict.sourceDir: the existing {dir} folder in the source
skills.import.manifestClash: The source's root folder already has a {file}, the same name as the file Ergo uses to track collections
skills.import.dirRenamed: Folder renamed from {from} to {to}; relative references from other skills in the collection that use the old name may break
skills.import.symlink: This folder is itself a symbolic link or junction, and imports don't follow links: {dir} (pick the real folder it points to)
skills.import.inDataDir: This folder is inside Ergo's data folder and can't be imported from: {dir}
skills.import.containsDataDir: Ergo's data folder is inside this folder, so it can't be imported as a whole: {dir}
skills.import.collectionRename: Renames of collection members go in collection.rename
skills.import.badName: New name {name} isn't allowed: use only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, up to 64 characters (it's also the folder name in the skills area)
skills.import.isSkill: This folder is itself a skill (it has a SKILL.md): import it as a single skill, or pick the folder above it as the collection
skills.import.membersRel: The members' subfolder must be a relative path under the root: {dir}
skills.import.noMembersDir: The root has no members subfolder {dir}
skills.import.depChanged: Dependency folder {dir} became a link or is no longer in the source; not imported
skills.import.freeName: Name “{name}” isn't lowercase letters, digits and hyphens; it's used as is (pi only warns and loads it anyway)
skills.import.linked: Dependency folder {dir} wasn't copied and is referenced at its original path: {target}
skills.read.noFrontmatter: SKILL.md doesn't start with frontmatter (name and description between ---)
skills.read.emptyName: The name in SKILL.md is empty
skills.read.nameTooLong: Skill name is too long (over {max} characters)
skills.read.controlChars: The skill name contains control characters
skills.read.noDescription: SKILL.md's frontmatter has no description (saying when to use it)
skills.import.tooBig: This folder is too large ({files} files, {kb} KB not counting dependency folders; the limit is {maxFiles} files, {maxMb} MB). A skill is a set of instructions and shouldn't be this big
skills.import.dirTaken: The skills area already has a folder called {dir}: move it away first, or import with a new name
skills.import.dirTakenNormalized: The skills area already has a folder called {dir} (what {source} becomes once normalized): move it away first, or import with a new name
skills.import.strayRenames: {names} in the renames aren't skills in this collection
skills.import.notDir: Not a folder: {dir} (pick the folder that contains SKILL.md)
skills.import.notDirCollection: Not a folder: {dir} (pick the folder that contains SKILL.md, or the collection's root folder)
skills.import.links: The source has symbolic links or junctions, and imports don't follow links, so nothing was imported: {links}. Replace them with real files and folders (or delete them), then import again
skills.import.linksMore: The source has symbolic links or junctions, and imports don't follow links, so nothing was imported: {links}… {n} in total. Replace them with real files and folders (or delete them), then import again
skills.import.dirConflict: {which} clashes with the folder of {owner} (the slash command is the folder name, so /{dir} would be ambiguous). You can import it with a new name (rename)
skills.import.dirNormalized: Folder name normalized to {dir} (originally {source}); the slash command is /{dir}
skills.conflict.text: {conflicts}. You can import with new names (rename for a single skill, collection.rename for a collection: old name → new name)
skills.secretary.problem: The settings file for {assistant}'s skills is {reason}; using the defaults for now
skills.secretary.missing: The skill library doesn't have {names} (import them on the skill library page first)
skills.dirProblem.noCommand: names with spaces can't be typed, so there's no slash command for now
skills.dirProblem.renameTo: you can rename the folder ({path}) to {fixed}
skills.dirProblem.renameAny: the folder name has no usable characters, so rename the folder
skills.dirProblem.notNormal: The folder name “{dir}” of {owner} isn't lowercase without spaces (the slash command is the folder name; {now}): {fix}. Ergo won't rename it automatically
skills.dirProblem.same: {owners} all have the folder name {dir}: /{dir} goes to {first}, and the others have no slash command (rename the folders)
